::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Google searching LaTeX commands?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/11905/google-searching-latex-commands), asked by [lowndrul](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/3762/lowndrul) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-02-24; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> Q: How can I best search the web for **exact** LaTeX commands (e.g., `\show` as opposed to `show`)?
>
> It appears that Google will not allow us to escape the `\` character. So, searches for `\show` are interpreted as `show`. Needless to say, results would be tremendously more helpful if the search were interpreted as the former. (note: `"\show"` doesn't help either)
>
> Q: Has anyone had success searching LaTeX commands using **other** search engine? More generally, does anyone know of search engines that are particularly well-suited for searching non-standard characters?
:::

My standard search phrase is "`tex latex <cmd>`."  For instance, [googling "`tex latex show`"](http://www.google.com/search?q=tex+latex+show&ie=utf-8&oe=utf-8&aq=t&rls=org.mozilla:en-US:official&client=firefox-a) leads me to a the "[ltxcmds](https://texfaq.org/FAQ-ltxcmds)" page from the TeX FAQ.
